To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
life’s origin follows from chemical and evolutionary processes that make heredity and evolution observable through living states.

life’s emergence requires (1) a high molecular complexity of the prebiotic chemical mixture, (2) a high degree of macromolecular crowedness, (3) non-covalent intermolecular forces and (4) Darwinian evolution of molecular surfaces.

life’s origins follow from chemical and Darwinial evolution, a high level of molecular complexity and crowdedness, and the action of non-covalent interactions that determine molecular recognition, cellular organization, and Darwinian evolution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physicochemical basis for life’s emergence, with the physicochemistry of living states, and with the molecular mechanisms of living cells.
the physicochemical principles that constrain life’s emergence to a physicochemical process under diurnal cycling gradients.
the physicochemical origin of life and its molecular basis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
life’s origins are not a mystery but a natural process that is observable and can be studied experimentally.
the living cell is a dynamic, non-equilibrium, self-reproducing and self-organizing system that is capable of adapting to environmental changes and that can evolve.
the origin of life is a consequence of the second law of Thermodynamics, and that the second law is a consequence of life.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

life emerges from the physicochemical properties of water and from the physico-chemical properties of macromolecules, which are the basis for the emergence of living cells and for the evolution of life on Earth.

life’s emergence follows from a physicochemical process of chemical and Darwinian coevolution, a high degree (complexity) of molecular diversity and crowding, and non-coevalent forces that determine molecular interactions and cellular organization.
life is an oscillating physicochemical process of chemical evolution, Darwinian evolution and Darwinian thresholds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the origin of life is a historical process that follows from the chemical and biological evolution of the Earth.
life is a cyclic physico-chemical process that makes Darwinian evolution observable.
life is a physicochemical process, not an information-based one.
